targets.title: Economic inequality, immigrants and selective solidarity: From perceived lack of opportunity to in-group favoritism.
targets.evidence_quote:
Our pre-registered (see Appendix B.1 for blinded version) survey design builds
upon and replicates Magni (2021) and Alesina, Miano and Stantcheva (2023)
with a quota-representative (age, gender, education, region) sample of the sur-
vey company Kantar.
targets.outcome_quote:
First, we find that priming respondents on high
inequality leads to a lower belief in meritocracy and thus confirm one central argu-
ment of Magni (2021). Second, we do not find that the inequality prime leads to
welfare chauvinistic redistribution preferences; the link suggested by Magni (2021)
does seem to be context-dependent.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The paper explicitly confirms the meritocracy step and rejects redistribution and welfare chauvinism links from the same original, with no overall all-or-nothing verdict.

targets.authors: Alesina, Alberto, Miano, Armando and Stantcheva, Stefanie
targets.title: Immigration and redistribution.
targets.evidence_quote:
Our pre-registered (see Appendix B.1 for blinded version) survey design builds
upon and replicates Magni (2021) and Alesina, Miano and Stantcheva (2023)
with a quota-representative (age, gender, education, region) sample of the sur-
vey company Kantar.
targets.outcome_quote:
Third, priming on immigration does not
make respondents support a reduction of redistribution as previously proposed by
Alesina, Miano and Stantcheva (2023); rather, it even decreases welfare chauvinis-
tic attitudes.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central immigration effect on redistribution fails; successful manipulation checks do not establish successful replication of that claim.

reasoning: Title and four authors verified on the primary preprint PDF. New German survey experiment tests two published originals. Main article pp. 1–23 includes references; appended online supplement is preserved in the extracted text. Original-data comparisons in supplement are descriptive checks rather than the central reanalysis purpose.
